category: answered elsewhere; confirmed or written up here
title: A118990(n) = 2^n A086906(n-1)
summary: For n >= 2 the number of singular symmetric +1/-1 matrices of size n is 2^n times the number of singular symmetric 0/1 matrices of size n-1 (sign normalisation of the first row and column plus one row reduction), proved in Lean for all n.
notes: Lean: A118990_eq n : card (A118990_pm (n+1)) = 2^(n+1) * card (A118990_zo n), Finsets of symmetric integer matrices with entries in {1,-1} / {0,1} and det = 0; bijection (s, B) -> s_0 diag(e) N diag(e) via Finset.card_nbij', det N = (-2)^n det B (A118990_det_norm). Axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Outside Lean: identification of the Finset cards with the OEIS terms (check.py brute force n <= 5, identity on all OEIS terms n = 2..10); no small term evaluated in Lean.

sources.cite: OpenAI, The sharp exponential rate of singularity for symmetric Bernoulli matrices (OpenAI math release family 239, 2026-10-03), Lemma 2.1
sources.what: Pr(det A_n = 0) = Pr(det B_(n-1) = 0) for uniform symmetric sign / 0-1 matrices, n >= 2; equivalent to the count identity; not formalised in the openai/math Lean collection

prior_art.note: Count form of OpenAI family 239 Lemma 2.1 (idea source). Neither OEIS entry states it; no Lean proof found elsewhere. This project's Lean proof is the first formalisation found.
